subject: Security decision flow: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Hayes <rachel@pulsehealth.com>, PulseHealth Procurement <procure@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Security decision flow: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC

Hi Rachel / PulseHealth team,

Thanks again for the time this morning — helpful to understand the clinical workflow and the audit window requirements. Quick recap + proposed decision flow so we can lock next steps: 

- Requirements you called out: BAA signed, SOC2 evidence (control excerpts for Logging & Access), quarterly audit windows, and a clearly scoped data retention policy.
- Options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest, needs BAA + data segmentation controls), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs, predictable throughput, best balance for you), Private VPC/on-prem (maximum isolation but longer onboarding + procurement).

Proposed decision flow (attached as a one-page grid):
1) If legal requires full data residency + on-prem SLA -> Private VPC or on-prem (procurement lead time ~8-12 weeks).
2) If residency OK but BAAs and SOC2 excerpts are mandatory -> Dedicated capacity (we can provide SOC2 snippets + scoped operational logs).
3) If residency not required and time-to-market is critical -> Hosted API with BAA and additional controls layered (token-level logging retention policy).

Action items I recommend:
- PulseHealth: confirm whether data must stay in your VPC or if a regional cloud is acceptable (Owner: Rachel; ETA: 12/10).
- Procurement: share any procurement schedule / standard contract clauses that would affect deployment mode (Owner: Procurement; ETA: 12/14).
- Redwood (Lauren/Grace): prepare SOC2 logging excerpt and initial BAA draft for review (Owner: Lauren; ETA: 12/09).

I've attached a draft BAA, our SOC2 excerpt, and a one-page decision grid to make tradeoffs explicit.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min follow-up once you confirm the residency constraint.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: PulseHealth_BAA_Draft.docx, redwood_soc2-snippet.pdf, deployment-decision-grid.xlsx

From: Rachel Hayes <rachel@pulsehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseHealth Procurement <procure@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Security decision flow: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC

Marcus — thanks for the summary, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from legal/procurement side: 

- PulseHealth requires a signed BAA in place before any PHI is processed. Residency: our initial preference is to keep data within our AWS account/VPC, but we can evaluate Dedicated capacity in a Redwood-managed VPC if the BAA and logging controls meet our requirements.
- SOC2: we need evidence for controls covering Logging, Access Management, and Change Management. Full SOC2 report is fine to provide redacted excerpts if necessary; procurement will want specific control IDs called out.
- Audit windows: we run semi-annual internal audits; we need a point of contact at Redwood for evidence handoff and a short SLA for responses (48–72 hours preferred).

Next steps from our side: procurement will confirm any non-standard contract language we need to flag (I expect that by 12/14). For now legal says: send the BAA + a one-page matrix mapping SOC2 controls to Redwood artifacts.

On timing — if Dedicated is an option and aligns with our residency preference, that's our likely path; Private on-prem is a last resort due to internal ops overhead.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Hayes
Head of IT Security | PulseHealth
rachel@pulsehealth.com

Adding the internal stuff here so we have a single action list.

Summary of what to pull together (I can take the SOC2 mapping):
- I will compile control excerpts for Logging (CC6.1), Access Management (CC5.2), and Change Management (CC7.4) and map them to the artifacts we can provide (logging schema, SLA for evidence handoff, incident response runbook). ETA EOD 12/09.
- Marcus, I'll draft a short BAA template we can send to PulseHealth as a starting point (we should avoid redlining until procurement raises specific clauses). ETA: 12/09 morning.
- Grace, can you confirm the typical lead time and runbook for spinning up a Dedicated capacity in a customer-managed VPC? I recall ~3–6 weeks for standard setup if infra approvals are fast; Private on-prem is much longer. We need a realistic calendar to share with Procurement.

Also attaching a quick decision grid (deployment-decision-grid.xlsx) that calls out timelines, control coverage, and expected procurement steps. We'll use this in the customer follow-up.

Rachel — appreciate the quick clarification. Short update and ask: 

- Lauren has compiled the SOC2 control mapping and I'm attaching that extract now (redwood_soc2-snippet.pdf). It maps CC5/CC6/CC7 to our artifacts and the expected evidence during an audit.
- Attached BAA draft is marked with the standard PHI handling and retention clauses.
- Timeline: if PulseHealth selects Dedicated in a customer-managed VPC, engineering confirms a pragmatic timeline of 3–5 weeks once procurement and network peering details are finalized. Private on-prem would add 8–12 weeks plus on-site validation. Hosted API with a signed BAA would allow us to start a limited pilot in 3–5 business days, but it may require additional contractual security appendices for your audit team.

Please confirm: would procurement like a single consolidated packet (BAA + SOC2 mapping + timeline + deployment grid) to start legal review? If yes, I'll send the consolidated packet and propose a 30-minute sync with procurement + our field security (Lauren) next week.

Thanks — looking forward to the next step.
